Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]
Etymology tree
French courge
Proto-Indo-European *-tós
Proto-Italic *-tosder.?
Late Latin -ittus
Old French -et
Middle French -et
French -etder.
French -ette
French courgettebor.
Portuguese curgete

    Borrowed from French courgette.[1][2]

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
     
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kuʁˈʒɛ.t͡ʃi/ [kuɦˈʒɛ.t͡ʃi]
    • (Brazil) IPA(key): /kuʁˈʒɛ.t͡ʃi/ [kuɦˈʒɛ.t͡ʃi]
      • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /kuɾˈʒɛ.t͡ʃi/
      • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /kuʁˈʒɛ.t͡ʃi/
      • (Caipira) IPA(key): /kuɻˈʒɛ.t͡ʃi/
      • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /kuʁˈʒɛ.te/ [kuɦˈʒɛ.te]
    • (Portugal) IPA(key): /kuɾˈʒɛ.tɨ/

    • Hyphenation: cur‧ge‧te

    Noun

    [edit]

    curgete f (plural curgetes)

    1. (Portugal) courgette, zucchini
      Synonym: (Brazil) abobrinha
